blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Confused Deputy and Task-Scoped Authority** in *Agent Security* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Security, § The Confused Deputy and Task-Scoped Authority
blocks.md: When the README names the private fixture as a search argument and the interface check confirms only that the runtime is permitted to search, the fixture leak repeats the shape of Hardy's compiler case with a query string in place of an output file. Because the runtime holds broader functional capability than any single request should exercise, prompt injection turns the confused deputy (definition \ref{dfn-confused-deputy}) from an occasional configuration mistake into the central failure mode of an agent.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Structural prompt injection matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.

questions.q: The section **The Confused Deputy and Task-Scoped Authority** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Injection turns the runtime into a confused deputy with a legitimate identity, so authorization must judge this request within this task, not the function name, argument types, or endpoint allowlist.

Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.
An agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and an external communication channel can be steered to exfiltrate, and removing any one leg breaks the attack path.
A defense is evaluated by system effects at the protected sink on whole eligible episodes, not by model text, and its overhead is priced in cost per accepted task.
